note: Review rules the local pack follows and prints into members' kits. Plain summaries; the sources are the final word.

link.find_place_id: Search your business name in Google's Place ID Finder and copy the ID it shows (it starts with ChIJ for most businesses).

rules: Never offer anything for a review: no discounts, freebies, gifts, entries or payment. Google bans incentives for posting a review and for changing or removing one.
Ask every customer the same way. Asking only the happy ones (review gating), or steering unhappy customers away from Google, is against Google's rules.
Never discourage or block negative reviews.
No reviews from yourself, family, staff or anyone paid to post them.
Reply to every review, good and bad, politely and without private details.
quotes: Google prohibits incentives such as payment, discounts, free goods and/or services in exchange for posting any review.
Discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews from customers is listed as fake engagement.

ftc.rule: 16 CFR Part 465, Trade Regulation Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials
bans: Fake reviews and testimonials, including ones written by AI or by people who never used the business.
Offering anything in exchange for a review that is conditioned on it being positive or negative.
Undisclosed reviews by owners, managers, staff or their relatives.
Company-controlled review websites that claim to be independent.
Review suppression: groundless legal threats, physical threats, intimidation or false accusations to stop or remove a negative review.
Buying or selling fake followers or views.
ftc.gating: The rule doesn't ban review gating by name, but FTC staff say gating can still be deceptive under the FTC Act, and Google bans it outright.
ftc.penalties: The FTC can seek civil penalties against people who knowingly break the rule.

yelp.rule: Yelp asks businesses not to ask for Yelp reviews at all. Point customers to Google instead, and let Yelp reviews come on their own.
yelp.source_note: Yelp's support page was down when we checked; the rule is also reported at https://searchengineland.com/yelp-increasingly-cracking-review-solicitation-across-internet-286290

asks.timing: Ask on the same day, right after the job is done and the customer has seen the result. A second, gentle reminder 3 days later is fine; stop after that.
asks.wording: Ask everyone the same neutral question (how did we do?) and send the same link to all of them.
